findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty data instead of actual query results
findings.body: When organization feature 'use-table-widget-visualization' is enabled, tableResultComponent renders <TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} /> with hardcoded empty values, completely ignoring the `tableResults`/`result` variable that was fetched for the widget. Any dashboard widget table rendered under this feature flag will always display as empty regardless of the actual query results, which is a functional regression for anyone on this flag.

findings.title: Mutually-exclusive age/timestamp validation uses truthiness instead of presence checks
findings.body: validate_timestamp/validate_age check `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` to enforce that age and timestamp are mutually exclusive. Since `timestamp` has min_value=0 and age could legitimately be 0, a falsy-but-present value of 0 for either field will not be detected as 'present', so a payload containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: <n>` (or vice versa) will incorrectly pass validation instead of being rejected.

findings.title: Broad exception swallowing and non-serializable value passed to logger.extra in get_environment_info
findings.body: get_environment_info catches bare `Exception` around `issue.get_recommended_event()`/`get_environment()` and only logs at info level, silently hiding any underlying bug (e.g. nodestore errors) rather than surfacing it to Sentry. Additionally it logs `extra={"issue_id": issue.id, "error": e}` passing the raw exception object (not `str(e)`) into the logging extra dict, which can fail or lose information depending on the logging formatter/handler used downstream.

findings.title: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE trailing newline plus join('\n') produces double blank lines between issues
findings.body: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n"` already ends with a newline, but github/gitlab integration.py build the issue_list via `"\n".join([...])`, adding an additional newline between each entry. This produces a blank line between every bullet (and multiple trailing blank lines before the footer), which breaks the intended tight bullet list formatting in the rendered PR/MR comment (confirmed by the updated test expectations which now show blank lines between bullets).

findings.title: Global default for autofix automation tuning silently changed from 'low' to 'off'
findings.body: DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT (and the corresponding project option default in projectoptions/defaults.py) was changed from "low" to "off", which changes the default automated-autofix behavior for every project that hasn't explicitly configured this option. This is a production-wide behavior change bundled into a PR that is nominally about the Replays bulk-delete system; it should be confirmed this is an intentional, reviewed change and not an accidental revert/leftover from another branch.

findings.title: Refactor to useQuery drops staleTime/retry/refetchOnWindowFocus settings used by previous useApiQuery call
findings.body: The previous implementation used `useApiQuery` with `staleTime: 0, refetchOnWindowFocus: false, retry: false`. The refactored version uses a bare `useQuery` call without reproducing these options, so the hook now inherits the client's default caching/retry/refetch-on-focus behavior. This silently changes request frequency and retry semantics for trace item attribute key fetching (e.g. it may now retry failed requests and refetch on window focus, which was explicitly disabled before).

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before feature-flag gate, polluting metrics for disabled orgs
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is called unconditionally at the top of `post()`, before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)` check that can return a 404. This means every call to this endpoint — including from organizations without the feature enabled — generates an analytics event, even though the request is ultimately rejected, skewing usage metrics for this feature.
